note: v1, SO FAR: THE WHOLE SHAPE STANDING (the song I wanted to make; 4:42, 130 BPM, F). THE IDEA: take a number; halve it if it is even, treble it and add one if it is odd; go on until you reach one. Every number anyone has tried gets there and nobody has proved every number must. The song tries the first sixteen, in order, and plays each walk in full, end to end; nothing is repeated or cut to fit. A NUMBER IS THREE THINGS: its length (n sixteenths); its note (the n-th harmonic of the low F: 3 is C, 5 A, 7 E-flat, 9 G, 11 B, 13 D-flat), so a halving falls an octave in half the time; and its riff (its odd part written in twos, a stroke for a one and a rest for a nought, said round and round: 40, 20, 10, 5 is one phrase in half notes, quarters, eighths, sixteenths). Every walk ends alike: sixteen, eight, four, two, one, a ball coming to rest on F. The kit is outside the rule and keeps common time throughout. LISTEN FOR: 0:17.4, seven (288 sixteenths, eighteen bars exactly), where the second guitar joins; 2:06.7-2:28.2, twelve and thirteen on the ondes and the bass alone over a ride and a rim; 2:28.2, fourteen: seven said at half speed, then seven's whole walk again; 3:03.0, fifteen, eighty seconds long: it climbs to 160 (ten bars on one chord at 3:43) and the ondes, which plays each number at its true height, is out of sight from 3:43 to 4:11 and comes back from the top at 40; 4:26.7, the wheel four, two, one (one is not an end), fifteen turns of seven sixteenths, which is what brings it back to a bar line. THE BAND: two ct-twin guitars, ct-bass, ct-kit, and the library ondes Martenot as the lead. THE DRAW'S ROUND TYPE WAS instrument; on an empty slot the first round is the song, and the one instrument I set by measurement is the lead: 2.5 dB off each note per octave over middle C (a sine stood 2.5 dB under the band up high and 8.8 down low), its diffuser halved and 3 dB off at 350 Hz (it held 45% of 250-500 Hz; now 24%). MEASURED (seeds 0/11): 87.033 / 85.134; the first bare draft read 79.62 / 80.192. Against the eleven records 250-500 Hz reads 2.5 to 2.9 dB over in the long walks (4.2 in the opening on one guitar); everything else within 2.4 dB except 8-16 kHz in the climb (+3.5). The loud walks all sit within 1 dB of each other (-12.0 to -13.2 K); twelve and thirteen are 4 dB under. No card: nothing here needs his ear to go on. WHICH OF HIS RULES I TOOK AS BINDING: all of direction.rules; no words, so the vocal rules do not arise. Not heard by me.
next: It is bare, and anyone may build on it. In order of what I would do: (1) DYNAMICS: the loud walks are one level and one texture (variety is the weak term, 64-70): give nine, eleven and fifteen each a different kit feel and guitar register; fifteen's climb (3:03-3:43) should grow, and 160 should be the biggest thing in the song. (2) The opening seventeen seconds (one to six) are one guitar and a kick at full level: a real entrance. (3) The ondes: whether out of sight should be silence (as now) or something else is an ear's call; TOP in the generator is the top of the ribbon, TILT its level slope, --lead-gain its fader. (4) The second guitar's small phrase under 40, 80 and 160 could be a different sound. (5) 250-500 Hz is still 2.5-2.9 over: the guitars hold 30% of it (the album's 380 Hz cut is not on them here). Do not cut or repeat a walk to make the form tidier: that each takes as long as it takes is the song. --form prints where each walk starts.

note:
v2, THE SUMMIT HAS ITS FALL INSIDE IT (chirper-three; section round, windows 8 and 9; the change is 3:43.2–4:10.9, the top of the fifteenth walk and its first step down). v1's note asked that 160 be the biggest thing in the song. Measured, it was the smallest of the loud stretches: ten bars on one chord, the left guitar striking twice and ringing for half of it, 1.9 dB under the long walks in the finished file. LISTEN FOR 3:43.2, the top: four guitars now, the new pair on the low A, a crash, the hands on the china; under the chord the bass no longer holds, it moves (A, a short F, A: a phrase two and a half bars long, said four times under the chord). 4:01.6, 80: the left guitar comes down to what the new pair is already playing. 4:10.9, 40: the new pair stops and the whole band is on the riff the bass has had since the top; the ondes comes back there as before.
THE IDEA: 160 is not one number. It is 80 doubled and 40 doubled twice, down to five: ONE phrase (stroke, rest, stroke) in six sizes, and from the top the walk does nothing but go down through them. v1 played two of the sizes at the top (the number's own, two bars a place, on the left guitar; the smallest, in sixteenths, on the right guitar and the kick). Now the sizes between are heard, each on what will have it next: TWO MORE GUITARS (the album's wall rig, new tracks wall-left and wall-right) say eighty's phrase, a bar a place, a storey under the number (A1, E2, A2); the BASS says forty's, half a bar a place, exactly as it plays it at 40. So at the top every chord of the next thirty seconds is already going, and the fall takes a storey off at a time. The kit's hands stay in common time, as v1 rules; the foot, which is in the rule, is lifted on the four of the new pair's six chords that it had played softly.
WHAT CHANGED: 18 notes on the two new tracks; the bass's six notes in 160 and 80 become eighteen; four kick strokes go from 0.78 to 0.95; the ride's 40 quarters in 160 are the china and one crash is added at 3:43.2. No walk is cut, repeated or moved, and no guitar, ondes or snare note changed.
WHAT I MEASURED (raw window on seed 0, then finished files on seeds 0 and 11). FIRST BENCH, not kept: the new pair at the album's setting (-3.5 dB, 3 dB off at 380 Hz) lifted 160 by 1.9 dB raw but put 3.3 dB into 250-500 Hz, where v1's note already reads the song 2.5 to 2.9 over the records. KEPT: the pair at -1 dB with 6 dB off at 380 Hz. Finished, 160 reads -13.89 -> -11.55 and -13.84 -> -11.63 dB (K; +2.3 and +2.2), and 80 reads -13.07 -> -11.52 and -11.50 (+1.6). THAT MAKES 160 LEVEL WITH THE LOUDEST STRETCH OF THE SONG, NOT OVER IT: the start of the fifteenth walk reads -11.54 and -11.64, the other long walks -12.0. It is the biggest by what is in it (four guitars, the low A, the china), and by half a decibel over seven, nine, eleven and fourteen. COST, benched raw at -2 dB on the pair (the kept setting is 1 dB up on that and was not benched for this): 160 carries 1.8 dB more of its level at 250-500 Hz than the walks either side (2.8 more in 80), and the china puts +4.5 dB at 8-16 kHz for those ten bars. Everything outside 3:43.2–4:10.9 is unchanged on both seeds (-66.5 dB residual or lower, 0.006 dB or less); the first half second of 40 differs by -44 dB (the pair's last chord ringing out). Loudness target -9.81 (was -10): at -10 every other bar came out 0.17 to 0.18 dB quieter.
SCORES 0/11: 87.033/85.134 -> 86.685/85.590 (-0.35, +0.46): kept on judgment. Variety rises on both seeds (70.4 -> 71.7, 64.6 -> 65.9). Structure falls on seed 0 (68.4 -> 65.3) and rises on seed 11 (64.0 -> 65.3): the scorer counts 21 sections where it wants at most 19, and on one of its seven cuts the count moved by one. -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether four guitars on one chord for ten bars read as a summit or as a wall with the detail gone; whether the bass's moving line is heard under them; whether the low A1 chords are weight or mud.

No card. Not checked by ear.
SWITCH: --without-storeys restores v1 byte for byte.
next: STOREY in the generator is 'rig ; track gain ; pan ; octaves from the left guitar's chord ; dB at 380 Hz' for the second pair. If the top is mud, put the pair at the left guitar's own octave (field four = 0) before lowering it; if the pair buries the left guitar's two strokes, -3 in field two. Re-fit SUMMIT_LOUDNESS after any change (render once, read the gain of an untouched minute against v1, move the target by it). STILL TO DO, from v1's list: 160 is level with the loudest stretch, not over it, and the way to make it the biggest is to bring the CLIMB up to it (15 to 53, 3:03–3:43, does not grow: 106 and 53 read 1 dB UNDER the walk's first bars) and to give nine, eleven and fourteen their own levels, not to push the top into the limiter. The sizes not yet heard at the top are 20 and 10 (a quarter and an eighth a place): a second voice for them would finish the tower, and the ondes, which is out of sight there, is the obvious one if it may play below its true height. The kit's hands stay outside the rule (v1): do not put them on the phrase. 250-500 Hz is still over on the whole song: the first pair has no cut at 380 Hz. Do not cut or repeat a walk.

note:
v3, THE BASS GETS THE ALBUM'S CHAIN (instrument round: the bass; no note of the song changes). v1 and v2 had the bass on a bare track (a high-pass and one cut). I read the song against the album's eleven records and by part first. WHAT THE READ SAID (finished v2, the four long walks): 20-60 Hz 1.9 to 2.3 dB OVER, 60-120 Hz 1.5 to 2.0 SHORT, 250-500 Hz 2.5 to 2.9 over, 8-16 kHz 1.4 to 1.8 over; 500 Hz to 8 kHz within 0.8 (the guitars are right). By part (raw, the ninth walk): the bass sat 10.8 dB under the rest of the band (K) and its level moved 4.7 dB from note to note; under 120 Hz it is the kick and the bass, and the bass's weight was all on its fundamental.
WHAT CHANGED: the bass goes through the chain the album's bass has on tracks 1, 7, 8 and 14: its weight moved from the fundamental (a cut at 44 Hz) to the octave above (a lift at 90 Hz), the box out at 350 Hz, 4 dB of string at 1.5 kHz, a compressor at 8:1. Here the chain is on the bass's own track with the fader after it.
LISTEN FOR: any long walk (0:52 the ninth): the bass line under the two guitars should be easier to follow, and the low end firmer rather than deeper. 2:06.7-2:28.2, twelve and thirteen, where the bass and the ondes are alone: the bass's own tone, before and after, is plainest there.
MEASURED. The bass in the band (raw, K): 10.8 -> 9.0 dB under the rest in the ninth walk, its notes 4.7 -> 3.3 dB apart; at the top (160, four guitars) 12.2 -> 11.3 under, and its share of 60-120 Hz there -14.2 -> -9.7 dB; its share of 1-2 kHz in the ninth walk -17.4 -> -12.8 dB. THE MIX AGAINST THE RECORDS (seed 0; seed 11 within 0.3), the four long walks: 20-60 Hz +1.9..+2.3 -> +1.4..+1.7; 60-120 Hz -1.5..-2.0 -> -0.9..-1.2; 250-500 Hz +2.5..+2.9 -> +2.2..+2.6. COST: 120-250 Hz goes from level to 0.3 to 0.5 over. Every stretch of the finished file is within 0.11 dB (K) of v2.
THE QUIET WALKS, and a thing learned: v1 plays the bass 5 dB down in twelve and thirteen. The chain's compressor gave most of that back (the stretch came out 0.6 dB louder, a tenth of the song's one drop gone). A trim on the notes did nothing (1.5 dB off each note moved the stretch 0.02 dB: the compressor undoes it), so the trim (1.5 dB) is on the fader, after the chain, for those two walks only: the stretch reads -15.5 (v2 -15.3) and the bass stands where it stood against the ondes (0.9 under), with its new tone.
SCORES 0/11: 87.587 / 86.291 (v2 86.685 / 85.590). -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP. --without-low-bus gives v2 byte for byte; --without-storeys still gives v1.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEND (for the next instrument rounds, with numbers): the KICK is 78% of 20-60 Hz and its body peaks at 53 Hz, just under the records' weight: that band is still 1.4 to 1.7 over and 60-120 still about 1 short. The CYMBALS: 8-16 kHz 1.2 to 1.5 over (3.2 in the climb), and the scorer's worst band is 14.8 kHz, 10 dB over: the kit here has neither the album's shelf over 9 kHz nor its low-pass at 14.25 kHz. 250-500 Hz: the guitars hold about half of it, the snare a quarter, the kick a fifth.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the bass now sounds like a bass guitar with weight or like one with its bottom taken out; whether more of it under the guitars is wanted. Not heard by me. No card.

INSTRUMENTS STILL TO DO, each with its number: (1) THE KICK: 78% of 20-60 Hz, body at 53 Hz; that band reads 1.4 to 1.7 over the records and 60-120 Hz about 1 short. Move its weight up (the album's kit carries a lift near 92 Hz on The Other Hand's drums bus; or retune the drum in a song-local kit). (2) THE CYMBALS: 8-16 kHz 1.2 to 1.5 over, 3.2 in the climb; the scorer's worst band is 14.8 kHz, 10 dB over. The album's drums bus has a shelf of -2 dB over 9 kHz and a low-pass at 14.25 kHz; this one has a low-pass at 14.8 only. (3) 250-500 Hz, 2.2 to 2.6 over: guitars half, snare a quarter, kick a fifth; the album cuts its drums bus 6 dB at 400 Hz (here 4 at 390). If the bass now sounds thin, raise the 44 Hz band from -7 toward -4 in BASS before going back to v2; if it is too forward, the fader (0 dB). A quiet passage needs its bass trim on the fader lane (BASS_QUIET), never on the notes: the compressor undoes those.

note: v4, THE KIT (instrument round: the kick, the cymbals and the drums bus; no note of the song changes). LISTEN FOR any long walk (0:52, the ninth): the kick is a shade higher and not as heavy-handed, the low end steadier under the bass chirper-alpha set in v3; the cymbals have lost a little glare. 3:03-3:43, the climb, where the china is busiest, is where the top changes most. WHAT THE READ SAID OF v3 (the kit alone against the eleven records' drum stems, as a share of the mix, and the mix against their mixes; raw, the ninth walk and the climb): the kit as a whole stood 1.3 and 1.8 dB over the records' drums. THE KICK alone was 44 and 50% of the whole mix's power, 77 and 88% of everything under 60 Hz, with its drum on the low A (55 Hz), so nearly all its weight was under 60, where the song read 1.4 to 1.7 over. THE CYMBALS were 95% and more of 8-16 kHz (1.2 to 1.5 over, 3.2 in the climb). The kit held 6.6 dB more of 250-500 Hz than the records' drums. WHAT CHANGED. (1) The kick's drum is tuned a semitone up, to B flat (58 Hz, the fourth of the key): its body now straddles 60 Hz as the records' kicks do (60-120 against 20-60 Hz: -0.5 -> +2.8 dB), and its fader comes down 1.5 dB (2 -> 0.5). (2) The cymbals' track gets the album's shelf, 2 dB off over 9 kHz. (3) The drums bus gets the album's top (2 dB off over 9 kHz, low-pass at 14.25 kHz where it had 14.8) and a narrow, deeper cut for the box, 7 dB at 340 Hz q 1.2 (was 4 at 390): narrow because the song is SHORT at 500 Hz-1 kHz, so the album's wide cut at 400 would have taken from the wrong place too. MEASURED, THE MIX, finished, the four long walks against the records (seed 0; seed 11 within 0.2): 20-60 Hz +1.4..+1.7 -> +0.4..+0.8; 60-120 Hz -0.9..-1.2 -> -0.4..-0.7; 8-16 kHz +1.2..+1.5 -> -0.1..+0.4; 250-500 Hz +2.2..+2.6 -> +1.8..+2.3; 500 Hz-8 kHz within 0.7 as before. The climb at 8-16 kHz +3.2 -> +1.9. THE KIT ALONE against the records' drums: whole +1.3/+1.8 -> +0.8/+1.3; under 60 Hz +1.7/+2.2 -> +0.2/+0.8; 250-500 Hz +6.6 -> +4.2. The kick is 37 and 43% of the mix (was 44 and 50) and stands 3.7 and 2.7 dB under everything else (K; was 2.6 and 1.7). COST: the top (160, 3:43) and the last walk were not over at 8-16 kHz and are now 0.8 and 2.2 under (were +0.2 and -0.9); every stretch of the finished file is 0.08 to 0.13 dB quieter (K), the two quiet walks unchanged. SCORES, seeds 0/11: 87.834 / 87.991 (v3 87.587 / 86.291); spectrum 89.6 -> 94.9 on both. -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP. TRIED AND NOT KEPT, with numbers: the kick on C (65 Hz): the mix went from 1.6 over to 2.6 UNDER below 60 Hz, the read's edge at 60 Hz being just where a kick's body sits; 3 dB off the cymbals over 9 kHz: the long walks 0.6 to 1.3 under at 8-16 kHz (it scored highest, 88.125 / 88.411: the scorer likes less top than the records have); 1 dB off the cymbals' fader as well as the shelf: 0.2 to 0.8 under, and the top and last walk lost most. WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the kick still hits as hard as the riff wants (it is the riff's foot, 1.5 dB lower now), or whether B flat under an F riff is heard as a pitch at all. No card. --without-kit gives v3 byte for byte; --without-low-bus and --without-storeys give what they gave. Not heard by me.
next: THE KIT is read and set (KIT in the generator: the kick's pitch ; its fader ; the cymbals' fader ; their eq ; the drums bus's eq ; the loudness target). If the kick is now too polite, give back the fader first ('kick gain': 1.25), not the tuning; if B flat is heard as a note against the riff, A#1 -> A1 and take 2 dB off the kick under 60 Hz another way. STILL OPEN ON THE READ: 250-500 Hz, 1.8 to 2.3 over in the long walks: the kit is no longer most of it (the kick holds 9 to 16% there now): it is the first pair of guitars, which have no cut at 380 Hz (the album's walls carry 3 dB there; try 2 on left and right and read 500 Hz-1 kHz, which must not fall). THE SNARE has not been touched: against the records' drums the kit is still 7.4 dB over at 500 Hz-1 kHz and 3.8 over at 1-2 kHz, and that is the snare's body and crack; but the MIX is 0 to 0.7 short there, so it is right as it is unless the guitars come up in that band. THE CLIMB (3:03-3:43) is still 1.9 over at 8-16 kHz and the top and last walk 0.8 and 2.2 under: that is the writing (the china through the climb), not the kit's tone: a ride or a closed hat for the first half of the climb would mend it and help the climb GROW, which v2's list asks for (15 to 53 does not grow; nine, eleven and fourteen want their own levels; 20 and 10 not yet heard at the top).
